subject: Demo follow-up: model runway choices & qualification checklist
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@brightline.ai>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@brightline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Demo follow-up: model runway choices & qualification checklist

Hi Sarah / Alex —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap + our recommended next steps so the pilot can move fast into evaluation. I focused the shortlist on three candidates that map to the quality / latency / cost tradeoffs we discussed (search + summarization + contextual extraction use cases).

Recommended candidate shortlist (high-level rationale):

1) gravitas-6b-q4 (compact)
   - Why: best-in-class for sub-100ms token generation on a single A100 for your short-response flows; very low token cost.
   - Tradeoffs: modest drop on long-context summarization; surface-level hallucination risk for multi-step extraction (we recommend prompt guards).

2) helix-13b-int8 (balanced)
   - Why: strong quality across few-shot summarization and extraction; p95 latency ~150-220ms with batching; good middle ground for throughput and cost.
   - Tradeoffs: ~1.6x cost vs gravitas, but noticeably better on your longer prompt suite.

3) titan-40b-evo (high-quality)
   - Why: best quality for complex extraction/regression-sensitive prompts, maintains fidelity on edge cases.
   - Tradeoffs: highest cost and latency; recommend for narrow, high-value routes (e.g., final-step decisioning).

Key bench numbers (attached + links):
- Benchmarks file: benchmarks_20280914.csv (attached) — includes p50/p95 token latencies, tokens/sec, and estimated $/1k tokens under Redwood Dedicated and Hosted plans.
- Short prompt set (attached) — brightline_prompt_set_v1.zip: includes your test prompts + a small regression pack to watch for quality drift.

Immediate risks & mitigations:
- Regression risk on extraction prompts: add a small validation set (we included 150 edge-case prompts in the prompt pack) and run a 48-hour smoke to compare F1 / precision drop.
- Latency-sensitive paths: enable local KV caching on prefix prompts and configure a small dedicated pool (2 GPUs) for the gravitas route to stabilize p95.

Suggested next steps (3 actions):
1) You: confirm which 3 production routes to run in the pilot (we suggested: quick answers, long-form summarization, extraction) by EOD 9/15.
2) Redwood: provision a 48-hour smoke for each candidate (we’ll run both Hosted and Dedicated profiles and provide the bucketed latency/cost report).
3) Mutual Action Plan: we attached a draft MAP (mutual_action_plan_draft.docx) — please review and flag legal/procurement asks.

If that sounds good I’ll schedule a short follow-up on 9/18 to review the smoke results and pick a primary candidate for the pilot.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: model runway choices & qualification checklist

Thanks Naomi — useful summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we lock routes: 

1) For the gravitas-6b-q4 candidate: you mentioned sub-100ms token generation. Is that observed with single-request streaming (no batch)? Our quick-answers route will be single-request, strict p95 < 200ms SLA.
2) For titan-40b-evo: what’s the expected dedicated cost delta vs helix-13b-int8 for the same throughput? Ballpark is fine.
3) Security note: we’ll need to confirm that logs for the 48-hour smoke can be routed to our S3 bucket and that audit-level access is enabled. Can Redwood set that up for the smoke?

If you can answer those, we’ll confirm routes today. Also tagging Alex — he’s owning procurement questions and the MAP review.

—Sarah
Sarah Lin
Director of Product, BrightLine
sarah@brightline.ai

Hi Sarah — answering inline and adding ops details: 

> 1) gravitas single-request streaming latency?
- Observed: gravitas-6b-q4 single-request p95 ~85-110ms on an A100 with optimized kernels (no batching), consistent when KV prefix is cached. If you expect cold-starts we recommend a warm-up policy or a tiny reserved shard.

> 2) titan vs helix cost delta?
- Ballpark: titan-40b-evo ~3.5x the $/1k tokens vs helix-13b-int8 under Dedicated pricing assumptions (see benchmarks_20280914.csv). Under Hosted, the delta is slightly higher due to instance sizing. We’ll include exact numbers in the smoke report.

> 3) logs to BrightLine S3 + audit access?
- Yes — we can export inference logs (redwood-observed-requests, token-level traces) for the smoke to a pre-signed S3 path. We’ll also turn on audit logging for the MAP window. Need Alex’s S3 write role and target bucket path.

Operational suggestion (rollout + guardrails):
- Run the smoke for 48 hours per candidate with identical prompt set.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, extraction F1/precision, hallucination rate (false positives on extraction).
- Canary plan: 1% traffic to primary candidate for 72 hours, then 10%, then ramp. Configure automatic fallback to helix-13b-int8 if latency > 2x SLA or error rate > 1%.

I’ll start provisioning the smoke nodes once Alex confirms the S3 path and we get the OK on routes.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
